NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>The source shows one street-facing view: a stepped brick frontage, seven-bay dark cladding at left, two stacked recessed balconies, a narrow four-tier window, and an elevated glazed pavilion with projecting flat roof edges. CURRENT reproduces this arrangement and its main silhouette closely. The clearest discrepancies concern the lower balcony opening and pavilion framing. Rear elevations, building depth and concealed roof construction are unverified; the additional CURRENT views cannot establish their source fidelity or confirm concealed joints.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: The lower balcony glazing extends almost to the brick recess’s right edge. The source shows a substantial warm-colored right reveal between the window frame and brick corner, giving this opening appreciable depth.
action: Locally narrow and recess the lower balcony glazing, restoring the visible right reveal and overhead soffit. Preserve the balcony’s outer width and stepped brick outline.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: The elevated glazed pavilion has thinner perimeter framing and a shallower dark roof-to-glass band than the source. This weakens the heavy framed opening that defines the upper silhouette.
action: Thicken the visible pavilion perimeter posts and roof underside locally, reducing the glazing within the existing outer silhouette to match the source.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="front">problem: CURRENT brickwork reads as smooth, uniform orange courses. The source’s dominant brick surfaces have thinner-looking courses, irregular tonal variation and pronounced horizontal texture.
action: Adjust the brick material’s course proportions, color variation and relief on the visible frontage and boundary walls.</issue>
<keep>Seven vertical bays in the left dark-clad frontage.
Four stacked glazed sections in the narrow right-hand window.
The two balconies’ outer widths and vertical arrangement.
The stepped left edge of the main brick frontage.</keep>
